title: Your Coding Agent Is 6 Months Out of Date — Jakub Hojsan, Exa
talk_summary: Exa pitches a semantic search API for coding and review agents, arguing that model knowledge cutoffs leave agents blind to recent repo changes and dependency updates. The transferable mechanism is not just adding search, but explicitly instructing agents when to search and returning compact, traceable highlights instead of full pages.

takeaways.technique: Ground dependency/version diffs with upstream search
takeaways.what_they_do: When a PR diff bumps a dependency or version, the review agent is instructed to search the upstream repo/changelog and ground its review in the breaking-change evidence.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you have a diff that bumps a dependency or version, you might want to look at the upstream source to verify that this is actually true

takeaways.technique: Two-step tool adoption: tool plus trigger rules
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue that adding a search tool to the harness is insufficient; the agent also needs explicit rules for when to invoke it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: adding it to the harness is simply not enough. So, it's really a two-step process. It's instructing your agent when to use web search

takeaways.technique: Compact extracted highlights instead of full pages
takeaways.what_they_do: Search returns small query-relevant snippets extracted computationally at runtime, not whole pages and not an LLM synthesis step.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You're feeding it quite literally only 500 characters to answer the question.

takeaways.technique: Log search traces for review debugging
takeaways.what_they_do: The search tool returns the exact queries, sources, and highlights passed to the model so they can be sent to telemetry and inspected when something goes wrong.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You get the entire trace of what we looked for, the exact queries, the exact sources

takeaways.technique: Provider-agnostic search tool behind one API
takeaways.what_they_do: They expose one fixed search API/MCP so agents can use the same search interface regardless of which model provider is routed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have like one fixed API that you're calling instead of everything that the other model providers are using
